sources.title: Du Fu Thatched Cottage & the Famed Chengdu Poet's Park - China Highlights
sources.content:
Du Fu's Thatched Cottage is a 24-acre memorial park in Chengdu's western suburbs dedicated to the Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu (712-770 AD). The site combines historical significance with beautiful landscaping and serves as one of Chengdu's major cultural attractions.

Historical Context: Du Fu is regarded as one of China's greatest poets. He fled to Chengdu during the An Lushan Rebellion and wrote over 200 poems in his modest hut there. These works, created during times of personal hardship including war, family separation, and hunger, are celebrated as masterpieces of realistic poetry.

Practical Information:
Location & Address: Caotang Road, Qingyang District
Hours: May-October: 8am-8pm. November-April: 8am-6:30pm.
Admission: 50 RMB per person
Recommended Duration: 3 hours

What to See: The park features Exhibition Room and Hall of Odes with celebrity photos and poetry collections. The restored Thatched Cottage building. Pagoda of the Buddhas with Qing Dynasty foundations visible beneath glass floors. Ancient pottery and architectural remains. Orchid gardens and bamboo groves. Multiple pavilions and traditional bridges. Tea service available (98 RMB for two or 50 RMB per jin to take home).

Nearby Attractions: Jinli Street, Wuhou Temple, Wide and Narrow Alleys (Kuanzhai Xiangzi), Chunxi Road, Sanxingdui Museum, Jinsha Site Museum.

sources.title: Du Fu Thatched Cottage Chengdu Guide: Tickets, Tips & Highlights
sources.content:
Du Fu Thatched Cottage is a major cultural landmark in Chengdu located along the Huanhua Stream, spanning nearly 300 acres. It was the residence of Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu, who composed over 240 poems during his four-year stay there—approximately one-sixth of his total literary output.

Scenic Features: The landscape includes camphor groves, plum blossom gardens, orchid patches, and bamboo forests with traditional Sichuan timber architecture. Stone bridges span calm waters framed by willow trees, with lotus flowers visible in summer and vibrant red foliage in autumn.

Key attractions include: The Thatched Hut (a recreated straw-roofed house reflecting the poet's daily life), Huanhua Stream (featuring scenic stone bridges and seasonal flora), Bonsai Garden (displaying rockeries and miniature landscapes).

Cultural Sites: Hall of Great Elegance (features poetry exhibitions with murals and sculptures of 12 renowned poets), Gongbu Shrine (dedicated to Du Fu and other influential Sichuan poets), Tang Dynasty Relics Exhibition Hall (displays pottery, coins, and archaeological findings).

Visitor Experiences: The site offers poetry audio guides with QR codes, children's chorus performances blending classical verse with music, and cultural creativity shops selling crafts and offering calligraphy instruction.

Dining Options: Shu Daxia Hot Pot approximately ¥86 per person, Shixiangge around ¥49 per person.

Transportation: Metro Line 4 to Caotang Beilu Station (Exit B), then 10-15 minute walk. Bus Routes 19, 35, 58, 82, 151, 165, 170, 309, 319. Taxi: Request "Dù Fǔ Cǎo táng".

Admission Details: Cost ¥50 per person. Hours 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily (tickets sold until 5:00 PM). Best visited weekday mornings for fewer crowds.

Seasonal Recommendations: Spring offers flowering plants, summer provides cooling shade, autumn delivers golden ginkgo and red maples, while winter presents a serene atmosphere ideal for reflection and photography.

sources.title: How to Visit Du Fu Thatched Cottage in Chengdu (Tips, Photos & Map)
sources.content:
Du Fu Thatched Cottage is an idyllic 24-acre park and museum in honor of the Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu at the western outskirts of Chengdu, located at Flower Washing Brook. It is the former residence of the poet saint Du Fu who lived here for more than three years (759-765 AD), and he composed more than 240 poems in his thatched cottage.

Opening Hours: 8:00-20:00 from May to October, 8:00-18:30 from November to next April. General admission is 60 yuan, with free entry for seniors over 60.

Getting There: Take Metro Line 13 to Du Fu Thatched Cottage Station, exit C2, and walk westward for 400m. Alternatively, take bus 35, 58, 82, 151, 165, 170, 1024 or g74.

Travel Tips: Best Time to Visit: Spring (Mar-May) offers plum blossoms, cherry blossoms, and fresh greenery, while summer provides shady paths and cool breeze from Huanhua Stream. Duration: 2 to 3 hours walking leisurely. Bring water, sunscreen, and a small umbrella. The path is easy and good for families with kids.

Highlights: Visitors praise the tranquil atmosphere, lush greenery, and well-maintained historical structures.

sources.title: 杜甫草堂 - 百度百科
sources.content:
杜甫草堂位于四川省成都市青羊区，是唐代诗人杜甫流寓成都时的故居。该遗址占地近300亩，已被列为第一批全国重点文物保护单位。

历史沿革：唐肃宗乾元二年（759年），杜甫为避安史之乱进入四川。翌年春，他在友人帮助下于浣花溪畔修建茅屋居住。万里桥西一草堂，百花潭水即沧浪即指此处。杜甫在此居住近四年，创作诗歌240余首。

唐末诗人韦庄寻得遗址并重建茅屋。之后历代修葺扩建，明弘治十三年（1500年）和清嘉庆十六年（1811年）进行了重大重修。

建筑特点：草堂保留清代嘉庆时期的建筑格局。中轴线上依次排列照壁、正门、大廨、诗史堂、柴门、工部祠，两侧配以对称的回廊。整体呈现古朴典雅而又幽深静谧、秀丽清朗的特色，属混合式中国古典园林。

主要建筑：
诗史堂：中轴线主体建筑，陈列著名雕塑家刘开渠创作的杜甫塑像。
工部祠：因杜甫曾任检校工部员外郎得名。祠内有明、清石刻杜甫像，清代将黄庭坚、陆游配祀其中。
少陵草堂碑亭：茅草顶亭子，内立石碑镌刻少陵草堂四字，为果亲王允礼所书。
茅屋景区：依据杜诗描写和明代格局重建，展现诗人故居的田园风貌。
大雅堂：展示64平方米大型彩釉镶嵌磨漆壁画和12尊历代诗人雕塑。
万佛楼：2005年重建，位于东面楠木林中。

文物价值：草堂珍藏各类资料3万余册、文物2000余件，包括宋元明清历代杜诗精本、外文译本及朝鲜、日本汉刻本120多种。

保护措施：1961年列入第一批全国重点文物保护单位；1985年成立博物馆；2001年发掘唐代遗址；2006年评为4A级景区；2008年评为国家一级博物馆。

旅游信息：地址成都市青羊区青华路37号。门票50元/人。时间09:00-18:00（17:00停止售票）。

sources.title: 杜甫草堂旅游攻略 - 成都本地宝
sources.content:
杜甫草堂门票价格为60元。博物馆实行预约、错峰、限流票务措施，可提前14日预约购票。

优惠和免费政策：60周岁以上老年人凭身份证原件直接刷证入馆免费参观；6周岁以下或身高1.3米以下的儿童凭身份证、居民户口簿免费参观；残疾人凭有效证件实行免费。

开放时间：夏季（5月1日-10月31日）08:00至20:00；冬季（10月1日-4月30日）08:00至18:30，闭馆前60分钟停止售票。

建议游玩时间为3-4小时，最佳季节为四季皆宜，夏、秋两季最佳。

杜甫草堂占地300多亩，园内有香楠林、梅苑、兰园、翠竹苍松，整座祠宇既有诗情，又富画意。

交通方式：可乘坐公交19路、35路、58路、82路、151路、165路、170路、309路、319路前往，或乘坐地铁4号线到草堂北路地铁站步行1公里到达。

sources.title: Du Fu Thatched Cottage: Highlights to See, How to Visit
sources.content:
Located at Qinghua Road, Qingyang district, was the former residence of the famous poet Dufu in the Tang dynasty where He lived here for nearly four years and wrote more than 240 poems.

Essential Information: Entry Cost: 50 yuan. Hours: 8:00-19:00 (summer); 8:00-18:30 (winter). Duration: 2-3 hours. Optimal Season: Spring and autumn.

Historical Context: Du Fu (712-770) was a renowned Tang Dynasty poet known as the poem saint. He fled to Chengdu in 759 to escape conflict, constructing his cottage by the Huanhua river in 760. After his departure in 765, the structure deteriorated until poet Weizhuang rebuilt it during the late Tang period. The cottage was also restored later in the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties.

Main Structures to Visit:
Great Elegance Hall: Features colored glazed murals and 12 poet sculptures.
Great Hall: Houses a bronze Du Fu statue by sculptor Qian Shaowu.
Poetry History Hall: Displays over 1,400 poems reflecting Tang Dynasty society.
Ministry of Works Shrine: Honors Du Fu's government position.
Straw Gate: The original cottage entrance with calligraphy by Pan Tianshou.

Transportation Options: Downtown buses: Routes 19, 35, 58, 82, 151, 165, 170, 309, 319. From East Station: 30-35 minutes by taxi (~37-40 yuan). From North Station: 20-25 minutes (~40-50 yuan). From Shuangliu Airport: 30-35 minutes (~50-65 yuan).

Nearby Attractions: Jinli Ancient Street and Wuhou Temple complement visits to this cultural landmark.
